newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- Chief Executive designate Tung Chee-hwa, still pondering who to keep on after the handover, has met all 22 senior government officials except the head of the Monetary Authority, Joseph Yam, since under the Basic Law, it is not stated whether the position is considered a principal government post.

-- MING PAO -- Beijing was considering a proposal to limit the production of foreign brand beers in China to within 10 per cent of the total beer production in the country. Foreign investment in breweries would also be limited. There are more than 700 beer producers in China now.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Hongkong Telecom had transferred its paging department and more than 1,000 staff to another company. A person in charge of a paging service workers' association said 3,000 paging staff were on a blacklist which meant that once they were fired from their present jobs, they could not seek employment in the business again.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Several countries have promised to grant visa-free access to Hong Kong Special Administrative Region passport holders after the handover.

-- The average lifespan of Chinese intellectuals is getting shorter. Ten years ago the average life of the intellectuals in a Beijing district, "the Chinese Silicon Valley", was 58 years. Now it had fallen to 53 years. About 80 per cent of patients suffering from malignant tumours in Shanghai were intellectuals.

-- SING TAO -- Wong Tai Sin Temple has applied to the government to be authorised to conduct marriages. If the application is granted, it will be the first temple in China to hold Taoist-style marriage registration ceremonies, which include kowtowing nine times to the Taoist deity.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- A top Chinese official says China must end irrational production by state-owned mines, mills and factories if the sector is to stem multi-billion dollar losses.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Chinese Premier Li Peng has extended his influence over foreign policy by promoting a close associate to oversee Sino-U.S. relations, a key part of China's global strategy.
-- China Eastern Airlines has formally launched its Hong Kong initial public offering, with promises that proposed fare unification in China would do nothing but good for the carrier.
